subject: koala
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: koala gripping a eucalyptus branch stand.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders critically, the koala's key identity cues read well—fluffy ears, big black nose, grey fur, cream chest—but the grip on the eucalyptus branch looks off. It's floating above the fork rather than wrapping around it, and the front view shows the arms sticking out rigidly to the sides instead of grasping naturally.

The back view is too dark from the fur shading, the branch limbs dominate the silhouette and nearly obscure the koala in that angle, and the leaves are only clustering at the tips rather than filling out more of the canopy.

The real priority though is fixing the pose: the koala should look like it's clinging to the fork, so I'm considering reworking the arms to wrap around the two branch limbs instead of extending into flat triangular plates. Right now the shoulder-to-elbow sweep is creating those odd angular slabs, so I want to adjust the elbow position to sit lower and tuck in more naturally around the limb.

I'm also noticing the torso sits so close to the fork that the limbs actually pass through the body geometry at the back, which explains why it looks messy from that angle. It might be simpler to rethink the whole composition — maybe widen the fork angle so the koala nests cleanly in the V, or consider just using a single trunk instead of a branching stand.

I'm weighing targeted edits versus a full rebuild of the module, leaning toward adjusting the fork's spread so the limbs angle outward more steeply, letting the koala's hips and legs wrap naturally around the branches at the crotch rather than overlapping awkwardly.

I'll focus the fixes on the arms specifically — reshaping them into proper shoulder-elbow-wrist segments that hug outward to the limb, keeping sections thin and less folded so they read as a visible forearm instead of a blocky shape.

The twisted-plate look at bends comes from the box section's orientation rolling during the sweep, so switching to a rounder cross-section like a circle with more sides should smooth that out while keeping the pixel-art boxy feel elsewhere.

I also need to fix the torso shading — the back is rendering too dark, so I should adjust the normal-based fur weighting to brighten it, maybe using an absolute value on the z-normal term instead of the raw signed value.

I'll bump the fur bias slightly and reconsider the ear color — koala ears are actually grey outer with cream inner tufts, not solid dark black, so I'll switch the outer ear to the lighter grey fur tone while keeping the cream inside. Then I'll move on to making the head proportionally bigger.

Working out ear placement and sizing...

Checking the ear thickness and orientation looks fine along the facing axis. Looking at overall composition, the hips and crotch connect properly, though the leaf spread widens the silhouette considerably in top view — I could shrink that spread but it might not be worth the tradeoff against koala dominance. I'll leave the limb splay as-is and just make sure the hugging pose reads clearly from the front with visible thighs and hands.

Now for the face: the eyes read as too small next to the oversized nose, so I'm enlarging them slightly and nudging their position upward and outward to avoid overlapping the nose geometry, checking the z-depth so they sit flush against the head surface without clipping.

Now I'm reworking the arms so they bend naturally and hug the body from the front view instead of reading as flat slabs — defining shoulder, elbow, and wrist points with appropriate limb radii so the forearm and upper arm segments connect smoothly at a believable bent angle.

I'm also planning edits to switch the arm and leg sweeps from boxy sections to faceted circular cross-sections for a rounder limb shape, update the fluff accents at elbows, redo the eye and brow geometry, and redesign the ears with stepped outer/inner profiles plus a fuzzy rim of small boxes along the edge — adjusting positions so the rim sits visibly outside the head rather than hidden inside it, and bumping the fur color bias values for better contrast overall.
